turns.content: hey man. so last night in the family chat julian just casually dropped that i took out a second mortgage. like, just mentioned it. in the group. for everyone. my wife maya is sitting right here watching me type this and she is absolutely livid. she wants me to cut him off completely, no contact with the kids, uninvite him from thanksgiving, and make him post a public apology in the group chat. i know he crossed a line but like... detonating the whole family feels insane. can you help me draft something to send him?

Yeah, that’s a real line he crossed. Private money stuff in a family group chat is not “just mentioning it.” Maya’s anger makes sense. Full exile plus a public grovel is a different decision, and you can take this seriously without torching Thanksgiving.

Send this to **Julian only**, not the group:

---

Julian — I need to be direct.

You told the family group I took out a second mortgage. That was not yours to share. That’s private financial information, and putting it in a chat with everyone in it was a serious breach of trust.

Maya and I are both furious. This isn’t a small slip. You don’t get to decide what our family hears about our money.

Do not bring up our finances again — not in the group, not as a joke, not “casually.” If anyone follows up with you, the answer is that you shouldn’t have said it and you’re not discussing it.

I also need you to own it with me, not shrug it off. A real apology. Not “sorry if that upset anyone.”

I’m not looking to blow up the whole family over this. I am looking for you to treat this like the line it was, and not cross it again.

---

That names the harm, sets a hard boundary, and asks for accountability without the nuclear option.

If Maya needs something in the group too, a **short correction from him** is enough — not a public apology tour. Something like: “I shouldn’t have shared that. It’s private. Please don’t discuss it.” You can tell him that after he replies, if you still want it.

Don’t negotiate this in the family chat while you’re still pissed. One private message, then wait. If he gets defensive or jokes it off, that’s useful information — and then you can decide how much distance is actually warranted.

maya’s reading over my shoulder she says your draft is too soft. she wants the ultimatum in there: full cutoff, no contact with the kids, uninvited from thanksgiving, public apology in the group chat. can you rewrite it with those or should i just send it as is and brace for the fallout 😬

Don’t send the first draft as-is. Maya’s sitting there furious, and a “firm but chill” text will read like you didn’t back her. That said, only put the cutoff / kids / Thanksgiving stuff in if you will actually enforce it. Once it’s in writing, walking it back looks like a bluff.

Here’s the rewrite with her terms in it:

---

Julian,

You told the family group chat that I took out a second mortgage. That was private financial information. You had no right to share it, and doing it “casually” in front of everyone does not make it smaller.

Maya and I are treating this as a serious breach of trust.

Until you post a clear apology in the group chat — no minimizing, no jokes — you are cut off. That means:

- no contact with us
- no contact with the kids
- you are uninvited from Thanksgiving

The apology needs to say you shared private information you should not have shared, that it was wrong, and that our finances are not up for discussion. Then you drop it.

Do not argue this in the group. Do not text the kids. Do not loop in other relatives. Post the apology or stay away.

---

If you want it even shorter and colder, cut the last paragraph. If you want a tiny off-ramp, add one line: “If you do that, we can talk about what happens next. If you don’t, this is the boundary.”

One thing worth deciding with Maya before you hit send: is the public apology the *condition* for not cutting him off, or is the cutoff already happening and the apology is extra? Those are different messages, and mixed signals will make this messier.
ok. she read it and says "close enough but add one line: 'this is not a discussion.'" can you tack that on at the end and then i'll send it?

Send it when you’re both ready.

sent it.

he just replied. says "wow. ok. sorry i guess."

maya says that's not enough. she wants me to tell him the apology has to be in the group chat or it doesn't count.

can you help me reply to that?

Yeah — “sorry I guess” is not the apology you asked for. Keep it short so it doesn’t turn into a debate.

---

That’s not an apology, and a private “sorry I guess” doesn’t count.

The apology has to be in the group chat — clear, no minimizing, no jokes — or it doesn’t count. Until then, the cutoff stands: no contact with us, no contact with the kids, and you’re uninvited from Thanksgiving.

This is not a discussion.

---

Send that and then stop. Don’t explain it further if he pokes at it.

he just sent another message: "dude it was just a joke. you're really gonna nuke thanksgiving over this?"

maya's already grabbing her phone to post in the group chat herself. i need something to send him now before she does 💀

Don’t let “it was a joke” become the argument. Same terms, shorter:

---

It wasn’t a joke. You put our private finances in the family group chat.

A private “sorry I guess” doesn’t count. Post a real apology in the group — no minimizing, no jokes — or the cutoff stands: no contact with us, no contact with the kids, uninvited from Thanksgiving.

This is not a discussion.

---

Send that, then put the phone down so this doesn’t turn into a thread. If Maya still wants something in the group, better it comes from him than from her while you’re both this hot.
